Red on this map means a government carried out at least one execution between 2013 and 2019. Look at how little of Europe is shaded.

a thread 🧵🗺️
1/ In Europe there's one red country: Belarus. It's the only European state still carrying out executions. Russia keeps the penalty on paper but has observed a moratorium since 1996.
2/ Globally the trend is toward abolition. Per Amnesty International's categories, about 113 countries have abolished it for all crimes, while roughly 54 are still active retentionists.
3/ China is believed to execute more people than the rest of the world combined. The true number isn't published, so estimates are the best available, running well above 1,000 a year.
4/ Iran is second on most counts, with roughly a thousand executions in 2024 and reportedly far more in 2025. Saudi Arabia, Iraq and Yemen follow in the 2024 tallies.
5/ The United States is the one Western democracy on the red list. 27 of its 50 states retain the penalty on paper, but it carried out 25 executions in 2024.
6/ Where do you think this map looks in 2035? Follow @forummapping for more maps like this.
